name: Typology: Shadows and Substance in Scripture

objectives.text: Identify that a shadow shows the shape of something real but is not the real thing, as a picture of how some Old Testament things point ahead to Jesus
Retell the story of the Passover and name Jesus as the Lamb of God whom the Passover lamb pointed to
Describe how God saved Noah's family through the ark and how the New Testament uses this to picture salvation in Christ
Connect the manna God gave Israel in the wilderness to Jesus' teaching that he is the true Bread of Life
Explain from Jesus' own words that the whole Old Testament speaks about him
Describe how the layout and furniture of the tabernacle teach God's holiness and the need for a God-given way to approach him
Define type, antitype, shadow, and substance using the language of Colossians and Hebrews
Compare the bronze serpent lifted up in the wilderness with Jesus lifted up on the cross
Compare the life of Joseph with the life of Christ, tracing the pattern of rejection, suffering, exaltation, and the saving of others
Classify biblical types as persons, events, or institutions and give an example of each
Analyze the criteria for a valid biblical type, including real history, genuine correspondence, escalation in the fulfillment, and warrant from Scripture
Explain how Paul presents Adam as a type of Christ, the head of a new humanity
Explain the Reformed teaching that Old Testament believers were saved through faith in the promised Christ whom the types and sacrifices foreshadowed
Compare the priesthood of Aaron with the priesthood of Christ, showing where Christ fulfills and surpasses it
Explain why Hebrews presents Melchizedek as a type of Christ's eternal priesthood
Explain how the temple finds its fulfillment in Christ's body and in the people of God joined to him
Explain why the ceremonial laws that served as types are no longer binding now that Christ has fulfilled them
Analyze how Hebrews argues that the repeated animal sacrifices revealed their own insufficiency and pointed to Christ's single sacrifice
Construct a study of the Day of Atonement that traces each element of the ritual to its fulfillment in Christ
Analyze how the Gospels present Jesus as the true Israel who relives and fulfills Israel's exodus and wilderness testing
Evaluate the difference between reading a passage typologically and allegorizing it, using examples from church history and Scripture
Defend the Reformed tradition's Christ-centered reading of the Old Testament against objections, using the New Testament's own interpretation
Synthesize the New Testament's greater than pattern to show how Jesus is the greater Moses, David, Solomon, and Jonah who fulfills the offices of prophet, priest, and king

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (shadow concept, Passover, ark, manna, Luke 24, tabernacle, bronze serpent, Joseph, criteria for types, Aaron's priesthood, temple, Day of Atonement, allegory vs typology, Christ-centered reading, greater than pattern). Dropped the vague kindergarten picture item and replaced it with a concrete shadow and substance objective. Recast observe and name items with assessable verbs and moved manna to grade 2. Added missing competencies: defining type and antitype vocabulary, classifying kinds of types, Adam as type, Old Testament saints saved through the foreshadowed Christ, Melchizedek, expiry of ceremonial types, insufficiency of repeated sacrifices, and Jesus as true Israel. Narrowed Leviticus 16 to verses 15-22, added supporting passages, and anchored confessions only where they state the doctrine (WCF 1.9, 7.5, 8.6, 19.3, WSC Q23 and Q25, Heidelberg Q19 and Q31). Left covenant structure and metanarrative content to sibling sub-topics.
